Subject: Re: ACME VPC handoff - topology & acceptance criteria

John — thanks for the clear list. I've attached our acceptance checklist and the
updated topology diagram (we incremented the version after the last runbook pass).
Below is a concise acceptance plan and the artifacts we need from ACME to close
security sign-off.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-acceptance-checklist-v1.xlsx (Excel), topology-diagram-v2.png (image)

Acceptance plan (high level):
1) Pre-test: confirm IP allocations and ACLs (ACME provides allocation confirmation).
2) Control plane tests (Redwood):
   - Control plane auth: verify mTLS handshake and KMS-wrapped keys.
   - Placement: control plane endpoints reachable only from management CIDR.
3) Data plane tests (joint):
   - BGP peering establishment and failover (observe route propagation).
   - Egress isolation: verify requests to external KMS and telemetry endpoints use
     specified egress IPs.
4) Evidence collection: network captures (pcap snippets), BGP session logs,
   control-plane auth logs (masked), signed checklist from ACME.
5) Post-test: remediation window and cutover/rollback plan sign-off.

Key asks for ACME prior to test window:
- Confirm tenant IP ranges and NAT mappings in a reply.
- Provide point-of-contact and access window for your on-prem network team.
- Share any additional corporate firewall rules that might block MTLS/KMS traffic.

Proposed test window: Thu 2027-10-07 09:00-12:00 PT. If that works for ACME we
will provision a monitoring TAP and collect the artifacts above.

Kimberly / Irene: can you confirm the KMS integration validation steps and the
list of log artifacts we should send ACME for audit? Also flag any additional test
prereqs we should include in the checklist.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Vanessa / John — quick KMS/keys note:

- KMS: We will use envelope encryption. Redwood's control plane will call customer
  KMS for the DEK wrap/unwrap; we will provide a masked audit trail (request IDs,
  timestamps, and truncated key IDs). ACME security gets the mapping table and
  KMS call logs for the test window.
- Validation steps in the checklist (already in the XLS): ensure a KMS test vector
  where ACME returns a deliberate failure to exercise fallback behavior.

I've opened a tracking ticket for the test evidence collection: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/NETOPS-4821
Attach that to the runbook so ops knows to drop logs into the secure bucket.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

John — following up with the concrete test schedule and a short checklist operators
can run during the window. If ACME confirms the window we'll post the runbook in
the shared Drive link below.

Operator test checklist (short):
- Establish BGP session (ASNs and neighbor IPs as in topology-diagram-v2).
- Announce /24 from ACME to validate propagation; measure convergence time under 30s.
- Simulate control-plane failover: take one control endpoint out and observe KV
  cache warmup behavior in <2m.
- MTLS certificate rotate: verify connection succeeds with rotated certs (both sides).
- Verify telemetry egress uses IPs: 35.198.12.45, 35.198.12.46 (these will be whitelisted).

Drive link (runbook & artifacts): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c/topology-diagram-v2

Proposed final test window (updated): Fri 2027-10-08 09:00-13:00 PT (gives ACME one
additional day to confirm). Please confirm POC contact and NAT mappings by EOD 10/05.

Jonas Weber
Network Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
